Finding Summary: Product Detail has no functional quantity selector. incrementQuantity()/decrementQuantity() are never called from any live widget — the only call sites are inside fully commented-out dead code, and the quantity-display widget is likewise entirely commented out.
Impact: Add to Cart and Buy Now from the PDP always submit quantity=1, with no way for a user to select a larger quantity before purchasing. Direct revenue/UX impact.
Recommendation: Re-wire the quantity stepper UI to the existing cubit methods and pass the selected quantity into addItem/buyNow calls.

Finding Summary: Wishlist data is persisted only in a single global SharedPreferences key (wishlist_items_v1), and the WishlistCubit instance is created once at app root and never torn down or reloaded on logout/login.
Impact: If User A logs out and User B logs into the same device, User B sees and can silently mutate User A's wishlist — a cross-account data leak, the same class of session-bleed risk flagged in the auth review but here baked into persistent storage.
Recommendation: Scope the wishlist storage key per authenticated user ID, and reset/reload the WishlistCubit on every login/logout transition.

Finding Summary: ProductModel.stock is declared, initialized to 0, and never reassigned from the parsed variant JSON (unlike ProductDetailModel/ProductVariant, which correctly parse inventory.availableStock). AllProductsScreen's grid also never passes isOutOfStock: to AppProductCard even though the widget fully supports an out-of-stock badge/disabled state.
Impact: Sold-out products on the Dashboard/'All Products' grid show as fully purchasable with no client-side warning, leading to failed/rejected add-to-cart attempts and user confusion.
Recommendation: Parse stock from inventory.availableStock in ProductModel's fromJson, and wire isOutOfStock into the Dashboard/All Products grid cards.

Finding Summary: No pagination anywhere in the catalog. Dashboard's 'All Products' fetches one fixed page (limit:100) and Product Listing fetches one fixed page per category (page:1, limit:20) — neither has infinite scroll or 'load more'.
Impact: Catalogs/categories larger than these caps have products that are permanently unreachable by browsing.
Recommendation: Implement infinite scroll / load-more pagination on both the All Products grid and the category listing screen.

Finding Summary: _resolveCategoryUuids expands a tapped category into every descendant UUID, then a for loop awaits _fetchProducts once per descendant sequentially.
Impact: A category tree with many subcategories fires that many sequential round-trips before the screen renders, each still capped at 20 products (compounds F-04), producing slow, incomplete listings.
Recommendation: Fetch all descendant category UUIDs in a single batched request (or parallelize with Future.wait) instead of sequential per-category awaits.

Finding Summary: loadHome() contains a leftover debug line, ((raw['data'] as Map)['data'] as List).first, which throws StateError whenever the API correctly returns zero products for page 1. That throw is caught by the same try/catch used for real network failures.
Impact: A genuinely empty catalog page falls back to showing old cached products instead of an accurate 'no products available' state, misrepresenting real inventory to the user.
Recommendation: Remove the leftover debug .first access entirely; distinguish a legitimately empty response from an actual fetch failure.

Finding Summary: HomeCubit, ProductDetailCubit, and ProductListingCubit all call GetIt.I<ApiClient>() directly inside their methods instead of taking dependencies via constructor injection, unlike CartCubit/WishlistCubit/CategoriesCubit which correctly use @injectable with a repository/use-case layer. None of the three are registered in injection.config.dart.
Impact: Impossible to unit test these three cubits with a mocked API client; inconsistent architecture makes onboarding and future maintenance harder, and increases risk of divergent error-handling patterns.
Recommendation: Refactor these three cubits to accept a repository/use-case dependency via constructor injection and register them with @injectable, matching the rest of the codebase.

Finding Summary: getCachedProducts returns cached data of any age with only a cosmetic 'cached Xh ago' label — there is no logic that treats old cache as invalid (no TTL/expiry).
Impact: Under the rate-limit fallback path, a stale price/stock/discount can be shown indefinitely across repeated 429s, risking users acting on outdated pricing.
Recommendation: Add a TTL to the cache service and treat expired entries as a cache miss, falling through to an explicit stale-data warning instead of silent indefinite reuse.

Finding Summary: The pattern 'await cartCubit.addItem(...); final error = cartCubit.state.error;' is repeated at three call sites reading global, unscoped error/isAddingItem fields on the app-wide CartCubit singleton.
Impact: Because these fields are shared app-wide, an unrelated cart operation resolving in the gap between the await and the read can show the wrong error message on an unrelated screen.
Recommendation: Have addItem return a typed result (success/failure + message) directly from the call rather than reading it back off shared mutable cubit state.

Finding Summary: onAddToCart() and onBuyNow() are empty and unused (real buttons bypass them, harmless), but onSeeAllReviews() is also empty and IS wired to the live 'See All Reviews' tap.
Impact: Tapping 'See All Reviews' silently does nothing, a visible dead-end in the UI.
Recommendation: Implement onSeeAllReviews() to navigate to a full reviews list/screen, or remove the affordance if not yet supported.

Finding Summary: 'Buy Now' has no double-tap guard, unlike 'Add to Cart' (properly disabled via AppButton's isLoading driven by cartState.isAddingItem). _buyNow calls context.push(AppRoutes.payment, ...) with no async gate.
Impact: A fast double-tap can push the Payment screen twice, potentially causing duplicate payment intents or confusing back-stack behavior.
Recommendation: Add the same loading/disabled guard used on Add to Cart to the Buy Now button.

Finding Summary: incrementQuantity/decrementQuantity never check availableStock (moot today per F-01 since the UI is dead), and switching to a lower-stock variant doesn't reclamp an already-elevated quantity.
Impact: Once F-01 is fixed, a user could select quantity 5 on a variant with stock 10, switch to a variant with stock 2, and still submit quantity 5.
Recommendation: Clamp the current quantity to the newly selected variant's availableStock whenever the variant changes.

Component/Layer: Wishlist — Move to Bag variant handling
Finding Summary: 'Move to Bag' resolves a variant server-side via WishlistRepository.resolveVariantUuid and adds it directly, unlike the PDP flow which requires explicit variant choice.
Impact: For a multi-variant product (size/color), the wrong variant can silently land in the cart without the user choosing it.
Recommendation: Require explicit variant selection (or default clearly and show which variant was chosen) before adding to cart from the wishlist.

Finding Summary: loadData() serializes two independent calls (_getCategories() then _getBrands()) instead of using Future.wait.
Impact: Needlessly slows first render of the Categories screen by the sum rather than the max of both request latencies.
Recommendation: Parallelize the two independent fetches with Future.wait.

Finding Summary: ProductListingCubit.toggleFavourite() is unused — the live screen correctly reads/writes the shared WishlistCubit directly — but the dead method's presence invites a future edit that would desync listing favourites from the real wishlist.
Impact: No current-day impact, but a maintenance trap that could reintroduce a wishlist desync bug later.
Recommendation: Delete the dead toggleFavourite() method.

Finding Summary: toggle()/remove() each await _prefs.setString(...) after their own synchronous emit(); in-memory state stays correct across rapid taps, but the two _persist() disk writes can race, and an app kill between an emit and its matching persist can leave the restored wishlist mismatched from what was last shown.
Impact: A user could see a heart filled in-session, kill the app before the disk write lands, and find the item missing from wishlist on relaunch.
Recommendation: Serialize persistence writes (e.g. via a write queue) or use a transactional storage approach so emitted state and persisted state can't diverge.

Component/Layer: Product Detail — dead mock data file
Finding Summary: product_mock_data.dart is confirmed unreferenced dead code anywhere in the project — unlike the auth review's KYC mock bug, it's unreachable, but still confusing clutter in data/models/.
Impact: Risk of a future developer mistakenly wiring it back in, or confusion about which data source is authoritative.
Recommendation: Delete the unused mock data file.

File:Line: all_products_screen.dart (~200 lines); home_screen.dart (451 of 1014 lines, ~44%); categories_cubit.dart (56 lines); product_categories_screen.dart (~90 lines); product_bottom_bar.dart; product_details_screen.dart; app_button.dart; product_info_section.dart; countdown_timer.dart; flashDealSection.dart (both fully dead)
Finding Summary: Large blocks of dead, commented-out code left in place across many files, including two entirely-dead widget files (countdown_timer.dart, flashDealSection.dart) — the live Dashboard renders 'Flash Deals' via a plain ProductRail with no countdown/urgency UI despite the label.
Impact: Significantly increases file size/noise and maintenance burden; misleads readers about what UI is actually live (e.g. 'Flash Deals' implies urgency messaging that doesn't exist).
Recommendation: Delete dead commented-out code and unused widget files; rely on git history for prior implementations. Either wire up real flash-deal countdown UI or rename the section to match actual behavior.

Finding Summary: HomeState.flashDeals is simply products.take(6) from the same general fetch as recommended — 'Flash Deals' and 'Recommended' aren't actually distinct curated lists today, just overlapping slices of one list.
Impact: Misleading merchandising — users see the same items twice under different labels with no actual deal/discount criteria applied.
Recommendation: Source Flash Deals from a genuinely distinct query (e.g. filtered by active discount/promotion) rather than slicing the general product list.

Finding Summary: AllProductsScreen._isInCart is dead — the live grid computes 'in cart' inline via context.watch<CartCubit>() instead.
Impact: Minor clutter/confusion about which code path is authoritative.
Recommendation: Delete the unused _isInCart method.
